name: CWA World Championship
epitaph: The CWA’s top belt in 2003 and 2004: Dizz is its first listed champion on 21 June 2003 and wins it three times that year, and the owner’s own character, Shannon Skanes, holds it briefly in October. Vigilante has it from 19 January 2004, the last holder its title history shows; the cards of 2004 then show Max Cameron taking it at Terror in the Aisles on 29 March and losing it to Leech at Outrage on 26 April, and Ash winning it at Blind Rage on 24 May and keeping it on 7 June.

name: CWA Inter-Continental/Superior Championship
epitaph: The Inter-Continental title of the CWA’s first summer, in 2003, which absorbed the Hardcore title on 5 July to become the Superior belt. Mach, Q, Shannon Skanes and Vigilante are its holders on the title history, and the cards of 2004 show The Moose taking it on 23 February, SinmaN on 26 April and Tommy Air on 24 May.

name: CWA Hardcore Championship
epitaph: A hardcore belt first awarded to Romeo Salvador at Hardcore Hell on 10 May 2003 and held by Leech and The Moose before it was merged into the Inter-Continental on 5 July. A second hardcore belt appears from 20 October 2003, with Max Cameron and Dante trading it and Leech holding it from 19 January 2004 until Shannon Skanes won it in a three-way on 22 March 2004.

events.title: cwa-association-2003-superior
events.note: Its own title history: the Hardcore belt was dissolved on 5 July when it was merged with the Inter-Continental to form the Superior title.

name: CWA World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The CWA’s World Tag Team belts in 2003: Eternal Nightmares won a four-team match on 17 May, and the titles passed through BOD twice, Full House, Northern Exposure and Los Especialistos before Dark Forces took them on 1 December and Reality and Dark Ice Symphony followed in January 2004; the cards then show Dark Forces taking the belts back on 22 March 2004 and keeping them on 24 May.

name: CWA Aerial Championship
epitaph: A cruiserweight belt that begins with 6Pac Dudley’s win in a Cruiserweight Rumble on 17 May 2003, becomes the Aerial title, is dissolved on 5 September and returns in December; the cards of 2004 show Myst holding it by 1 March and Gloria Lavin retiring it at Outrage on 26 April.

name: CWA Women’s Championship
epitaph: Floated as a possibility in the owner’s news post of 1 August 2003 and awarded on 11 August to Lickety Split/Scarlet Bitch. Demona Calaway took it on 30 September 2003 and holds it into March 2004.
